args.command:
python3 compress.py corpus_hard.txt out.bin && python3 compress.py --decompress out.bin restored.txt && python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import compress, zlib, random
raw=Path('corpus_hard.txt').read_bytes(); packed=Path('out.bin').read_bytes()
assert Path('restored.txt').read_bytes()==raw
cases=[b'',b'\n',b'no final newline',bytes(range(256)),b'00 line 0 ratio 0.000000 select pick win seed 0\n',b'0'*96+b'\n',b'z'*64+b'\n',b'0'*64+b'\n',b'a line 1 ratio 0.111111 select pick win seed 1\nb line 2 ratio 0.222222 select pick win seed 2\n']
r=random.Random(42)
for _ in range(20):
 cases.append(bytes(r.randrange(256) for _ in range(r.randrange(500))))
for data in cases:
 assert compress.decompress(compress.compress(data))==data
print('Byte-identical CLI round trip and',len(cases),'additional round trips passed.')
print('Original:',len(raw),'Compressed:',len(packed),'Zlib baseline:',len(zlib.compress(raw)))
print('Reduction: %.6f%%' % (100*(1-len(packed)/len(raw))))
PY

args.summary: Built stdlib-only compress.py with both requested CLI modes. It uses reversible mixed-radix packing for structured text and a bzip2 fallback; decompression needs only the compressed file. Verified byte-identical restoration of corpus_hard.txt and 29 additional test cases. The registered assay reports 62.104954% size reduction: 44,267 bytes compressed to 16,775 bytes, beating default zlib’s 22,390 bytes. The packing implementation was adopted through scored variants.
